information: Langtang Valley Base Trek is a moderate trek north of Kathmandu in Langtang National Park.
The maximum altitude reached on the standard trail is 3,870m (12,700ft) at Kyanjin Gompa.
Optional viewpoint hikes include Kyanjin Ri (4,773m) and Tsergo Ri (5,033m) for panoramic views.
The standard duration of the trek is 8 days, including 1 acclimatization day at Kyanjin Gompa.
additional_information: This is one of the closest trekking regions to Kathmandu, offering spectacular glaciers without extreme altitude risks.

information: The starting trailhead is Syabrubesi (1,503m), reached via an 8-hour drive from Kathmandu.
The ending point is Syabrubesi, from where trekkers drive back to Kathmandu.
The total round-trip distance is approximately 50 to 60 kilometers.
Trekkers walk an average of 5 to 7 hours per day, covering 5 to 12 kilometers daily.
Day 1: Kathmandu to Syabrubesi (8 hours drive, 122 km).
Day 2: Syabrubesi to Lama Hotel (6-7 hours, 10km, follow Langtang Khola).
Day 3: Lama Hotel to Langtang Village via Ghora Tabela (5-6 hours, 12km).
Day 4: Langtang Village to Kyanjin Gompa (3-4 hours, 5km, easy ascent).
Day 5: Acclimatization day at Kyanjin Gompa, hike Kyanjin Ri or Tsergo Ri (4-7 hours).
Day 6: Kyanjin Gompa to Langtang Village (3-4 hours, 5km).
Day 7: Langtang Village to Lama Hotel (5-6 hours, 12km).
Day 8: Lama Hotel to Syabrubesi to Kathmandu (5-6 hours walk, 8 hours drive).
additional_information: The trek is a linear out-and-back trail following the course of the Langtang Khola river.

information: Peaks visible include Langtang Lirung (7,234m), Langtang Ri (7,205m), Dorje Lakpa (6,966m), Loenpo Gang (6,979m), and Yala Peak (5,520m).
Kyanjin Ri (4,773m) and Tsergo Ri (5,033m) are the key viewpoints overlooking Langtang peaks and glaciers.
The trail follows the glacial Langtang Khola river and passes through pine and rhododendron forests.
Kyanjin Gompa is a spiritual Buddhist center featuring an ancient local monastery.
additional_information: Memorial chortens in Langtang Village commemorate the victims of the devastating 2015 earthquake avalanche.

information: Syabrubesi (1,503m) is the motorable trailhead village with basic shops, electricity, and transport hubs.
Bamboo (1,960m) and Rimche (2,400m) are small forest settlements with basic teahouses.
Lama Hotel (2,480m) is a key forest settlement and standard first overnight stop.
Ghora Tabela (3,000m) is a valley opening point with basic lodges and yak pastures.
Langtang Village (3,430m) is a quiet rebuilt village nestled in Langtang Lirung foothills.
Kyanjin Gompa (3,870m) is the final destination, spiritual center, and acclimatization hub.
additional_information: Langtang Village was completely destroyed by an avalanche in the 2015 earthquake and has since been rebuilt nearby.

information: Local tea houses (20-30 lodges) are available along the entire route from Syabrubesi to Kyanjin Gompa.
Basic twin-sharing rooms are standard.
Toilets are Western-style in lower sections and squat-style in higher sections (shared).
Hot showers (solar/gas) are available below 2,500m (fee NPR 200-400).
additional_information: Hot showers become very limited, lukewarm, or unavailable above 3,500m due to freezing temperatures.

information: Tea houses serve traditional Dal Bhat, pasta, noodle soups, potatoes, and bread.
Kyanjin Gompa features a local government cheese factory producing Swiss-style yak cheese.
Tap water is unsafe; use water purification tablets/filters or buy boiled water (NPR 100-200 per liter).
additional_information: Yak cheese is a local specialty and highly recommended source of protein for trekkers.

information: A Langtang National Park entry permit is required, costing NPR 3,000 for foreigners.
A Trekkers' Information Management System (TIMS) card is required, costing USD 20 for individual travelers.
Permits can be purchased on arrival in Syabrubesi or at the park entry checkpoint.
additional_information: Checkpoints exist at Dunche and Syabrubesi; keep printed permits easily accessible.

information: NTC and Ncell have basic coverage up to Ghora Tabela, but it becomes weak/non-existent above.
Wi-Fi is available at Kyanjin Gompa teahouses for a fee (NPR 300-500), but is slow and limited.
Electricity charging for devices is available at tea houses (fee $2-3/device).
additional_information: Mobile signals are highly weather-dependent; satellite phones are available at Kyanjin Gompa in emergencies.

information: Best seasons: Spring (March-May) for blooming rhododendrons, Autumn (September-November) for stable weather/clear skies.
Winter (December-February) brings heavy snow, freezing temperatures, and path closures above Langtang Village.
Monsoon (June-August) makes trails slippery, introduces leeches, and increases landslide risks.
additional_information: Spring offers the warmest daytime trekking temperatures, while autumn provides the crispest clear views.

information: No hospitals or medical clinics exist along the trek route.
Basic first aid supplies are available at village health posts, but they are sparsely stocked.
Kathmandu hospitals are the primary destination for emergency medical care.
additional_information: Trekkers must carry a comprehensive personal first aid kit containing altitude medication.

information: Helicopter evacuation costs $3,000-$5,000 USD depending on weather, requiring insurance covering up to 5,100m.
Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) is a moderate risk above 3,000m; rise slowly and drink 3-4 liters of water daily.
Rescue landing points are designated at Lama Hotel, Ghora Tabela, Langtang Village, and Kyanjin Gompa.
additional_information: Langtang Valley is narrow, meaning helicopter rescue is highly dependent on clear visibility and low wind.

information: Syabrubesi starting point is reached by an 8-hour drive from Kathmandu (122 km) along winding mountain roads.
Transport options: public/shared bus ($15-20 USD) or private jeep ($80-120 USD).
Helicopter charter return is available from Kyanjin Gompa to Kathmandu ($1,275 USD per person shared).
additional_information: The road from Kathmandu to Dunche/Syabrubesi can be rough and is frequently affected by monsoonal landslides.

faq.question: What is the maximum altitude on Langtang Valley Trek?
faq.answer: 3,870 meters (12,795 feet) at Kyanjin Gompa. Optional hikes: Kyanjin Ri (4,773m), Tsergo Ri (5,033m)

faq.question: How many days does Langtang Valley Trek take?
faq.answer: 8 days standard from Kathmandu, 7 days minimum possible

faq.question: What permits are required for Langtang Valley Trek?
faq.answer: Langtang National Park Permit (NPR 3,000) and TIMS Card (NPR 2,000 green/independent). New rule may not require TIMS - check current regulations

faq.question: Is Langtang Valley Trek difficult?
faq.answer: Moderate - suitable for most trekkers with reasonable fitness. 5-7 hours walking daily

faq.question: What is the total distance of Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: 50-60 km round trip from Syabrubesi to Kyanjin Gompa

faq.question: Can I get altitude sickness on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, moderate risk above 3,000m. Maximum 3,870m at Kyanjin. Acclimatization day essential

faq.question: When is the best time for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Spring (March-May) and Autumn (September-November) - best visibility, stable weather

faq.question: Do I need a guide for Langtang Valley Trek?
faq.answer: New rule: Guide is mandatory. TIMS card requires trekking agency or guide

faq.question: How much does Langtang Valley Trek cost?
faq.answer: $550-700 per person from Kathmandu, excluding international flights

faq.question: Are there tea houses on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, 20-30 tea houses throughout route with basic rooms and meals

faq.question: Is meat available on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Only below Lama Hotel (2,480m). Above that, mostly vegetarian due to no refrigeration

faq.question: Can I drink tap water on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: No - must boil, purify with tablets, or UV sterilizer. Buy boiled water (USD 1-3/liter)

faq.question: Is Wi-Fi available on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes limited at Kyanjin Gompa (fee). No Wi-Fi below Lama Hotel

faq.question: How much does helicopter evacuation cost?
faq.answer: $3,000-5,000 USD. Insurance must cover 5,000m+ altitude evacuation

faq.question: What should I pack for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Warm layers, good boots, rain gear, water purification, first aid kit, headlamp, trekking poles recommended

faq.question: Do I need trekking poles?
faq.answer: Recommended for steep descents, especially Lama Hotel to Syabrubesi section

faq.question: Can I charge my phone on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, electricity available throughout (fee $2-3/device), mostly solar power

faq.question: Are hot showers available on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes below 2,500m (fee NPR 200-400). Limited above, cold water only above 3,500m

faq.question: What mountains can I see from Kyanjin Gompa?
faq.answer: Langtang Lirung (7,234m), Langtang II, Yala Peak (5,520m), Dorje Lakpa (6,966m)

faq.question: What mountains can I see from Kyanjin Ri?
faq.answer: Full Langtang range: Langtang Lirung, Dorje Lakpa, Yala Peak, Changbu, Yubra Peak

faq.question: What mountains can I see from Tsergo Ri?
faq.answer: Panoramic Langtang range and Shishapangma (8,027m) in Tibet

faq.question: Is Langtang Trek safer than Everest Base Camp?
faq.answer: Yes - max altitude 3,870m vs 5,364m, lower altitude sickness risk, shorter trek

faq.question: Can I do Langtang Trek in winter?
faq.answer: Yes, but cold temperatures and possible snow above 3,500m. Less crowded, clear views

faq.question: How do I get to Syabrubesi from Kathmandu?
faq.answer: 8-hour drive, 122 km, mountainous road. Shared bus $15-20, private jeep $80-120

faq.question: What is the difference between Kyanjin Gompa and Kyanjin Ri?
faq.answer: Kyanjin Gompa (3,870m) is village/monastery. Kyanjin Ri (4,773m) is viewpoint 3-4-hour hike above

faq.question: Are there monkeys on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: No monkeys. Rare wildlife includes Himalayan thar, snow leopard (extremely rare)

faq.question: Can I see rhododendrons on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, rhododendron forests 2,500-3,500m, bloom in spring (March-May)

faq.question: Is there a health clinic on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: No health posts on route. Serious cases need helicopter evacuation to Kathmandu

faq.question: What emergency number for trekking in Nepal?
faq.answer: Police 100, Tourist Police 1144, Healthcare First Helicopter +977 9801360911

faq.question: Can I trek Langtang without prior experience?
faq.answer: Yes, no technical sections needed. Good physical fitness essential, 5-7 hours daily walking

faq.question: What is the altitude of Kyanjin Gompa?
faq.answer: 3,870 meters (12,795 feet)

faq.question: What is the altitude of Langtang Village?
faq.answer: 3,430 meters (11,253 feet)

faq.question: Is Langtang Trek suitable for beginners?
faq.answer: Yes, moderate difficulty with no technical climbing. Good fitness and preparation essential

faq.question: How many liters of water should I drink daily?
faq.answer: 3-4 liters to prevent dehydration and altitude sickness

faq.question: Can I bring my own tent for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Not necessary - tea houses available everywhere. Camping only for special group arrangements

faq.question: What toilet facilities are on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Western-style below, squat toilets above. Shared facilities, sanitation generally decent

faq.question: Is Dal Bhat free on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Often unlimited at many tea houses - traditional 'food for infinity'

faq.question: Can I see snow leopards on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Extremely rare - snow leopards inhabit area but sightings virtually impossible for trekkers

faq.question: What is the best footwear for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Sturdy waterproof trekking boots with good ankle support and grip

faq.question: Do I need sun protection on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Essential - high altitude UV exposure. Sunscreen SPF 50+, sunglasses, hat mandatory

faq.question: Can I use credit cards on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: No cash only. Carry NPR (Nepali Rupees) - no ATMs on trail

faq.question: What is the walking time daily on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Average 5-7 hours, 8-12 km per day depending on section

faq.question: Is Langtang Trek crowded?
faq.answer: Less crowded than EBC/ABC. Spring and autumn busiest. Winter less crowded

faq.question: Can I do Langtang Trek solo?
faq.answer: New rule: Guide mandatory. Book through trekking agency for safety and permits

faq.question: What insurance do I need for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Must cover trekking to 5,000m+ and helicopter evacuation ($3,000-5,000)

faq.question: Is there mobile network on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, NTC coverage from Lama Hotel onward. Limited above, weather dependent

faq.question: What is the temperature at Kyanjin in winter?
faq.answer: -5°C to -15°C at night, can drop lower. Daytime 5-10°C

faq.question: Can I shower at Kyanjin Gompa?
faq.answer: No hot showers at Kyanjin. Cold water only, not recommended due to cold

faq.question: What is the lowest point on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Kathmandu at 1,400 meters (4,593 feet). Syabrubesi at 1,503m is trek starting point

faq.question: How steep is the climb to Kyanjin Ri?
faq.answer: From Kyanjin Gompa, 900m ascent in 3-4 hours. Moderate climb, manageable for most

faq.question: Can I see sunrise from Kyanjin Gompa?
faq.answer: Yes, but Kyanjin Ri is better sunrise viewpoint. Kyanjin Gompa offers sunrise over valley

faq.question: Do I need a headlamp for Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Essential - early morning hikes, evening movement, limited electricity after certain hours

faq.question: What is the food cost on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: $20-30/day average. Increases with altitude (2-3x at Kyanjin vs Syabrubesi)

faq.question: Can babies/young children do Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Not recommended below 10-12 years. Altitude 3,870m moderate risk for young children

faq.question: What is unique about Langtang Village?
faq.answer: Rebuilt after 1934 earthquake and 2015 avalanche. Quiet village in foothills of Langtang Lirung

faq.question: Is there a cheese factory on Langtang Trek?
faq.answer: Yes, Kyanjin Cheese Factory produces traditional yak cheese - local specialty

faq.question: What memorials are in Langtang Village?
faq.answer: 1934 earthquake memorial and 2015 avalanche memorial (during 2015 Nepal earthquake)
